title: Pool dynamics — many articles to one estimate
notes: Group C holds the cross-article boundary: the relevance safety net, the weight formula's three multipliers, logit pooling and its clamp, the CI and its widening, and the settlement override with aggregation-time revalidation. Everything here runs on already-collapsed article signals, so a Group C movement is a pooling change, not an extraction one.

cases.name: an off-topic-only pool abstains instead of estimating
cases.notes: One article at relevance 0.2 gives relevance_mass 0.04, below relevance_weight_floor (0.05). The pipeline must answer "couldn't answer" rather than report a confident stance drawn from tangential coverage.

cases.name: the relevance floor is a sum, so tangential volume buys past it
cases.notes: Three articles, each as tangential as C1's single one (relevance 0.2), sum to relevance_mass 0.12 and clear the floor — the safety net is a mass test, not a per-article test. The resulting estimate is thin (evidence_mass 0.072 against a decisiveness_floor of 0.5) and self-reports as such through a widened CI.

cases.name: relevance enters squared, so a half-relevant dissenter pulls a quarter as hard
cases.notes: Two articles identical but for relevance (1.0 vs 0.5) and stance (-0.8 vs +0.8). The convex application means the on-topic negative carries 4× the weight of the tangential positive, and the pool lands clearly negative rather than near zero.

cases.name: one recency half-life halves an article's weight
cases.notes: recency_half_life_days is 7. The 2026-07-25 article is exactly one half-life older than the frozen clock's 2026-08-01, so its weight multiplier is 0.5 and the fresh dissenter wins.

cases.name: a very old article decays to the recency floor, not to nothing
cases.notes: An article from 2026-01-01 is ~30 half-lives old; the decay is floored at recency_floor (0.02) so ancient coverage still counts a little instead of dropping out silently.

cases.name: an undated article cannot outweigh a dated one
cases.notes: Fixed by the R3 bundle (retro#366): recency_weight used to return a neutral 1.0 when the date was missing, so an article that never said when it was written beat an honest dated three-week-old report 50-to-1 and the pool read +0.784 toward it. An undated article now decays straight to recency_floor, which is where the dated 2026-01-01 article already sat: both weigh 0.012, they cancel, and the mean is 0.0. Missing metadata can no longer raise influence — the invariant below states that directly.

cases.name: thin evidence widens the interval instead of forcing an abstention
cases.notes: A single opinion-class source carries weight 0.25, half the decisiveness_floor (0.5), so deficit is 0.5 and up to thin_evidence_ci_inflation (0.45) of probability-space half-width is added symmetrically. defer_on_thin_evidence is off in prod, so the answer is a low-confidence estimate rather than a refusal.

cases.name: the logit clamp bounds an absolute stance short of the boundary
cases.notes: logit_clamp (0.01) keeps log-odds finite, so a lone source at stance +1.0 pools to +0.98, never +1.0. Any change to the clamp shows up here first.

cases.name: four unanimous hedged sources report a zero-width interval
cases.notes: The CI is computed from disagreement only. Four sources that all say +0.4 at certainty 0.5 disagree by nothing, so the interval collapses to a point — the estimator claims total precision on evidence it has itself classified as hedged. F16's unanimity floor is the fix. FIXED (retro#365, F16): widen_ci_for_unresolved_dispersion floors the band at 1.96*sigma/sqrt(n_eff), so these four effective sources publish width 0.196 instead of 0.0. Paired with B11 (n_eff 1, width 0.392) the two invariants pin the decay property: one effective source pays the full floor, four pay half.

cases.name: six echoing sources buy a tight interval on one story
cases.notes: Six articles carrying essentially the same claim (one mild dissenter) shrink the standard error by √n even though there is one underlying story, not six independent observations. This is the √N attack F2 (story clustering) and F16 (effective-N) exist to blunt; the case is here so their PRs can point at the number they moved.

known_bad.expected_behavior: Six copies of one story are one observation. Clustering should collapse them before the CI is computed, so the interval reflects independent evidence rather than syndication volume.

cases.name: two dated settlements pin the estimate to the boundary
cases.notes: settlement_min_sources is 2. Two articles each reporting the outcome as an accomplished fact, dated and settlement-grade, pass aggregation-time revalidation and pin the mean to +settlement_stance (0.94) with a tight asymmetric band — pooling alone could never reach there.

cases.name: valid settlements in both directions suppress the pin
cases.notes: The deadline has passed, so an undated "it never happened" vote is anchored by the closed window while the other article dates the occurrence inside it. Both votes are individually valid and they contradict — one extraction is provably wrong. Facts are not decided by outvoting: no pin, the pooled mean stands, and the conflict is logged for a human.

cases.name: settlements dated after the deadline are demoted at aggregation time
cases.notes: Both articles report an occurrence, both are dated — but dated 2026-07-20, three weeks after the claim's 2026-07-01 deadline. An occurrence outside the window contradicts the claim rather than settling it, so both votes are demoted to ordinary evidence and no pin fires. The demotion is invisible on the response beyond settled=false; the per-vote reasons are logged.

cases.name: undated foreclosures with no known deadline never pin
cases.notes: The F-35 / Netanyahu background-history class on the negative side: two articles assert the outcome is impossible, neither dates a foreclosing event, and the claim has no deadline whose expiry could serve as the anchor instead. Both votes are demoted; the pool still reads strongly negative, it is just not declared settled.

cases.name: equal-weight row volume buys a tight interval on one row's worth of evidence
cases.notes: F16's dispersion floor decays as 1.96*sigma/sqrt(n_eff), and n_eff is caller-controllable. Kish blocks NEAR-WEIGHTLESS padding beside a strong row (that pool keeps n_eff ~= 1), but not this shape: twelve IDENTICAL low-mass rows are perfectly equal-weight, so n_eff equals the row COUNT while the pool carries only about one strong row's worth of evidence mass. The interval then reports the number of rows rather than the weight behind them. This is the 76x fan-out shape already measured in the funnel work (news-indexer#193/#194, daatan#1231/#1232), not a hypothetical. Held at twelve articles because the runner gives each article index its own title vocabulary and only twelve exist; at the prod-shaped fifty the published width falls to ~2.8pp (retro#382's table), which rounds to 1pp and is invisible in daatan. Distinct from C10, which is the same collapse driven by SYNDICATION of strong rows (F2) rather than by low-mass volume.

known_bad.expected_behavior: Twelve rows carrying one row's worth of mass must not buy a twelve-row-tight interval. The published width should not fall below the single-source floor (~0.392, i.e. 19.6pp) on row volume alone. retro#382 records the measured mitigation as min(n_eff, k) with k = sum(min(w_i, decisiveness_floor)) / decisiveness_floor, verified a no-op on all five headline F16 cases (C9, B11, B15, B3, C10); it is the contingency now that retro#355 story clustering has landed but is shipped inert (cluster_downweight_exponent = 0.0), so nothing yet collapses volume before n_eff is computed.

cases.name: an off-topic pool still publishes the settlement pin it carries
cases.notes: retro#396. system-model §6.2 fixes one publish-time precedence — settlement pin > impossibility pin > abstention > glide > pooled estimate — but aggregate_pool evaluated the three abstention reasons first and returned early, so a pool tripping any of them could never publish a pin however well-founded. Four articles at relevance 0.1 give relevance_mass 0.04, under relevance_weight_floor (0.05): off-topic by the safety net's own measure. Two of them are dated, settlement-grade accomplished-fact reports attributed to Polymarket, so they keep the cited_probability premium (4.0) through enforce_anchor_provenance and carry 0.12 each — 0.24 combined, clear of settlement_quality_floor (0.20). A settled fact does not need a topically-dense pool to be true. Before the fix this answered all_articles_off_topic with articles_used 0 and discarded the settlement; it now publishes the pin, and the pool's thinness stays visible in evidence_mass rather than in the estimate. That the settling rows need the x4 anchor premium to get here is the point, not a contrivance: with any ordinary class the quality floor already nests inside the relevance floor, which is why the inversion never produced an incident.

cases.name: the same off-topic pool abstains when its settling votes are too weak to pin
cases.notes: The guard that keeps C16's ordering honest, and the reason hoisting the settlement decision above the abstention gate is not a loosening. Identical to C16 except the two settling sources carry neutral credibility, so the winning direction's combined weight is 0.08 against settlement_quality_floor's 0.20 (retro#279): the pin is suppressed and the abstention stands. 'This pool is unusable' and 'this pin is unusable' are two questions with two thresholds — retro#396 reordered them, it did not merge them.
